name: Question 3
problem: Which of the following represents the set $S=[-1,1]\times [0,1]$ in the Cartesian plane?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B={(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B}
$$

In this case, the set

$$
S=[-1,1]\times [0,1]
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
S={(x,y)\,:\,x\in [-1,1],\,y\in [0,1]}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{0}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $0$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
{S}_{0}={(0,y)\,:\,y\in [0,1]}
$$

We can represent ${S}_{0}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094658/assets/1cc30fcc7543bfbbf8c5c59d1436eb3b1a0799d60c9ad1d899957e8fd17d58ab.png)

Now, consider a general ${S}_{i}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals some $i\in [-1,1]$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any real number in the interval $[0,1].$

$$
{S}_{i}={(i,y)\,:\,y\in [0,1]}
$$

For each $i\in [-1,1],$ ${S}_{i}$ is a vertical line segment from the point $(i,0)$ to the point $(i,1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14094658/assets/494c9d77b0ff339b90792270c9d641054a03a2918e3c56a93747b42a77ee3ccf.png)

Our Cartesian product $S$ is the union of these subsets over $I=[-1,1]:$

$$
S={⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i}.
$$

As $i$ runs over $I,$ these line segments sweep the following rectangle that represents the union ${⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i}:$
